title: Recovering silver. Preserving silicon.
shortTitle: Silver recovery from silicon solar cells
summary: Two complementary laser routes recover valuable silver as bulk material or nanoparticles, with selective targeting informed by machine vision.
problem: Silver contacts are valuable, but separating them from a silicon solar cell requires control over both material removal and substrate damage. The desired recovered product also changes the processing strategy.
approach: Developed ultraviolet picosecond ablation for particle generation and infrared processing for selective debonding. Compared processing environments and characterized recovered material using microscopy, elemental analysis, and optical spectroscopy.
contribution: Led the first-author studies, developed processing conditions, characterized material response, and connected selective laser processing with image-derived targeting workflows.
results: Published complementary approaches for recovering bulk silver and silver nanoparticles. The work connects laser parameter selection to the form of the recovered material and the response of the remaining substrate.
takeaway: Choose the removal mechanism around the desired product: interfacial debonding for bulk recovery, or ablation for particle generation.

title: Separating layers. Keeping what matters.
summary: A continuous-wave laser process removes photovoltaic backsheet through the glass side while preserving the glass and silicon wafer.
problem: Photovoltaic modules combine glass, silicon, encapsulants, and polymer backsheets. Separating a target layer requires controlling heat across the entire stack.
approach: Used 1070 nm continuous-wave irradiation through the glass side to induce localized heating and interfacial delamination. Combined experiments with thermal analysis to distinguish useful delamination from excessive heating.
contribution: Led process development and first-author publication, connecting experimental process windows with thermal modeling and material characterization.
results: Demonstrated backsheet removal while preserving tempered glass and the silicon wafer. Raman, FTIR, optical, and electrical characterization evaluated the recovered materials and device integrity.
takeaway: A useful process window must account for heat flow through adjacent layers, as well as the response directly under the beam.

title: From an image to a laser scan path.
summary: Image segmentation identifies metallic contacts on irregular solar-cell fragments and converts their geometry into selective laser scan paths.
problem: Manual targeting becomes difficult when photovoltaic fragments have different shapes and electrode patterns. Automation must turn pixel-level predictions into usable processing geometry.
approach: Developed convolutional-neural-network segmentation, image preprocessing, line and contour extraction, and vectorization. Connected the extracted geometry with galvo-compatible laser workflows.
contribution: Developed scientific image-processing and segmentation workflows in Python and OpenCV and translated detected material features into vector scan paths.
results: The application reference reports greater than 98% pixel-level segmentation accuracy for the target electrode-detection task. The associated first-author paper demonstrates deep learning integrated with selective silver recovery. This is a task-specific segmentation result, not a claim of overall production yield.
takeaway: A vision model becomes an engineering tool when its output can drive a repeatable physical process.

title: One contact material. Two recovery routes.
shortTitle: Silver recovery from CIGS solar cells
summary: Ultraviolet picosecond ablation and infrared nanosecond debonding offer different routes to recover silver from CIGS cells.
problem: CIGS photovoltaics contain valuable silver contacts on a multilayer device. Recovery methods must account for the contact, underlying structure, and desired recovered form.
approach: Compared UV picosecond ablation and IR nanosecond debonding, including processing in air and water. Used SEM and EDS to examine recovered material and remaining device structures.
contribution: Led experimental process development and the first-author study, comparing removal mechanisms and relating processing conditions to morphology and composition.
results: Demonstrated silver recovery through both ablation and debonding. The published study shows how wavelength, pulse duration, and processing environment can be selected for nanoparticle generation or bulk recovery.
takeaway: Changing pulse duration and environment can change the recovery pathway, even when the target material stays the same.

title: Connecting growth, structure, and properties.
summary: Hands-on experimental research spanning pulsed laser deposition, single-crystal growth, vacuum systems, and materials characterization.
problem: Understanding electronic and energy materials requires repeatable sample preparation and a clear connection between growth conditions and measured properties.
approach: Used pulsed laser deposition, high-vacuum processing, and single-crystal growth. Combined structural, surface, compositional, and transport measurements to evaluate the resulting materials.
contribution: Worked as a Research Fellow at IIT Delhi from December 2019 to July 2022. Operated and troubleshot deposition and characterization equipment and developed repeatable experimental workflows.
results: Built experience connecting thin-film and crystal-growth conditions with structural, electronic, magnetic, and electrochemical behavior. This experience underpins my approach to process development and metrology.
takeaway: Reliable process conclusions start with reliable samples and measurements across more than one length scale.
methods: XRD, SEM, TEM, XPS and PPMS

title: Engineering a transparent conducting film.
summary: Sb-doped SnO₂ films fabricated by thermal evaporation and post-oxidation, evaluated through structural, optical, and electrical measurements.
problem: A transparent conducting oxide needs useful optical transmission and electrical properties. Both depend on how the precursor film is deposited and oxidized.
approach: Fabricated metallic precursor layers using thermal evaporation and converted them through controlled post-oxidation. Used XRD, optical transmission, and four-probe electrical measurements to compare the resulting films.
contribution: Conducted MSc research at IIT Ropar and served as first author on the resulting AIP Conference Proceedings paper.
results: Published a fabrication and characterization study of 5 wt% Sb-doped SnO₂ thin films, connecting post-oxidation and precursor thickness with structure, transparency, and resistivity.
takeaway: Deposition and post-treatment are coupled process steps; the final film must be assessed optically and electrically as well as structurally.
